items.title: Nancy Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: By the time I went with John, he had Ramsey Lewis, Gene Harris, The Three Sounds... he had so many wonderful artists that he nurtured

ctx.x: Was being in that area of the country, was the music different from when you moved to New York? Did you notice a —

No. No I think we were all pretty much on a — at that time — we’re talking about time that made the difference, as opposed to where you were. Maybe if you were in, if I’d have been in Kansas City I might have sung more blues or R&B. But what I heard as a child, was Little Jimmy Scott, Nat Cole, Bull Moose Jackson, Laverne Baker, Ruth Brown, Dinah. Basically male influences first. Louis Jordan and the Tympani Five. My father was the one who bought records. Consequently what I heard were male influences. I found…

did such a good job for George, that just opened the door. By the time I went with John, he had Ramsey Lewis, Gene Harris, The Three Sounds, he had Cannonball, I mean he had so many wonderful artists that he nurtured and made sure that they took care of the business and did wonderful things for them. So the object of my strategy was, if I’m going to do this, the only person who I would trust to help and be there for me would be John Levy.

items.title: Nancy Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I love Gene Harris of the Three Sounds. We never got a chance to work together too often, but when we did, it was memorable.

ctx.x: Did that kind of camaraderie give you a different feeling? Do you miss that sort of thing today? It just seems like such a different sense of time and place.

It wasn’t, not really. I don’t change from day to day. I am what I am, and that’s whether I was working with Cannonball or Shearing or Ramsey [Lewis]. I love Gene Harris of the Three Sounds. We never got a chance to work together too often, but when we did, it was memorable. But I don’t change up, just because it’s different people. I’m still who I am and do what I do and was very blessed and fortunate that it is what it is.
Do you remember anything about the shows at the Apollo?
